name: I Want to Hold Your Hand

podcast.body: A number one smash hit that was dominant on the charts in the winter of 1964. This song's success notably kept Leslie Gore's proto-feminist anthem "You Don't Own Me" from reaching the number one spot, forcing it to peak at number two. "Stuck behind the Beatles number one smash I want to hold your hand."

podcast.body: Despite being one of their biggest songs at the time, "I Want to Hold Your Hand" was conspicuously absent from the 11-song setlist performed by The Beatles at their Vancouver concert on August 22, 1964. "which oddly didn't include I want to hold your hand one of their biggest songs at the time."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: In March of 1964, this song was replaced at the number one spot on the Hot 100 by The Beatles' own hit, "She Loves You," marking the first time any act in Hot 100 history replaced themselves at number one. "In March of 1964, the Fab Four's She Loves You replaced their own hit I Want to Hold Your Hand in the number one spot."

podcast.body: This song broke The Beatles in America, spending seven weeks at the top of the Hot 100, the most of any single in 1964. It initiated an "unrepeated" streak of three consecutive number one hits, directly followed by "She Loves You" and "Can't Buy Me Love." This period marked the dizzying peak of American Beatlemania. "The song that broke them in America, I want to hold your hand, spent seven weeks on top."
